data.title: Meta Stocks Slip Although Muse Reaches Seven Inference Platforms
data.description:
Social-media and AI developer Meta Platforms expanded access to its AI technology with Muse Spark Open, while shares traded at $730.445, down approximately 0.85%, at around 10:04 a.m. ET on October 16. Developers now have more ways to use Meta's models outside its apps. The investment question is straightforward: how does wider adoption turn into earnings? The release does not quantify its expected revenue contribution.

Meta's announcement lists seven hosted-inference partners and describes a model with 816 billion total parameters, 42 billion active parameters and a one-million-token context window. Meta says it can also run on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios. Downloadable weights give developers more control, but the company's license terms place limits on commercial use. Wider access does not mean unrestricted access. And while active parameters represent roughly 5.1% of the total, that ratio alone says little about actual operating costs.

The valuation snapshot puts Meta 15.75% below its $866.96 GF Value estimate, suggesting potential upside if the assumptions behind that estimate hold. That gap is a valuation signal, not a guaranteed return. For shareholders, the next checkpoints are developer adoption, commercial agreements and measurable improvements in Meta's products. Getting the model into more hands opens doors. Turning that reach into profitable growth is the harder test.

data.title: Meta Muse continues to see increased adoption, though overall rates are low: BNP
data.description:
The strong interest in Meta Platform's Muse artificial intelligence agent does not seem to be slowing down, BNP Paribas said on Friday.

Citing third-party data analysis, the investment firm said the app, which overtook OpenAI's ChatGPT at the top of the App Store, has generated more than 10.4M downloads so far, BNP analyst Nick Jones said in a note to clients. Downloads peaked on day 12 of the release and have since stabilized in an upward trend, the analyst added. Jones has an Outperform rating and an $885 price target on Muse.

“While Muse Wonder is mainly targeting enterprises and developers, it will also power Meta Muse, initially for paid subscribers, which could help increase adoption and engagement,” Jones wrote in a note to clients. “Compared with other AI platforms, Muse’s early U.S. downloads surpassed Sora and ChatGPT, which is not surprising given its massive install base for Instagram, WhatsApp, and Facebook.”

Delving deeper, Jones said engagement for Muse is still early, and users are "predominantly" men, and younger people have “relatively low adoption” of the app. As such, it's unlikely to be a threat in the near-term to vertical marketplaces due to “still-nascent” adoption and a few other issues.

“In terms of monetization, as of now, Meta is charging partners small transaction fees. Muse is free for the basic tier and offers monthly subscriptions for higher usage to maximize adoption and engagement,” Jones added. “But we believe long-term monetization remains a question mark for investors—we see a path where advertising could be compelling as engagement builds.”

Events that investors will need to pay attention to include how well OpenAI's Dots (which is believed to be geared towards the enterprise) does, as well as when other companies such as Google , SpaceX , and others launch their AI agents, Jones added.

data.title: Week's Best: Stocks You Can't Refuse in Trump Accounts — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Barron's Advisor Staff

The Treasury Department has already dramatically expanded these tax-deferred investment accounts for children in two different ways. First, it is automatically enrolling millions of children under age 18, the department announced Oct. 1. Second, it is expanding how certain individuals can contribute to them — and what can be contributed. Large donors can contribute stocks to groups of account holders, who generally must hold the shares for a minimum of five years — and can't refuse the donations. The Treasury Department and the Internal Revenue Service are seeking public comment about whether there should be more exceptions to those rules.

Among other most-read wealth management articles this week:

Investment advisors' moves for rising rates. Higher borrowing costs are reshaping the investment landscape. For investors, this shift brings both opportunity and risk. Cash and bonds now offer more income, but rising yields can pressure longer-duration bonds and many stocks. Barron's asked a panel of investment advisors: What portfolio changes are you making as interest rates rise? They told us they are moving to short- and intermediate-term bonds, adding Treasury inflation-protected securities, and rebalancing stock portfolios to avoid concentration risk.

Schwab earnings shine, but stock falls. Charles Schwab's profit jumped during the third quarter as the brokerage firm's customers added billions of dollars to their accounts and increasingly used Schwab's lending and wealth management services. The stock fell 3% on Thursday, however. One analyst said Schwab's net interest margin of 3.04% was a modest disappointment, but he still rates the shares a Buy.

Big RBC team heads to Indivisible Partners. A wealth management team that worked at RBC Wealth Management for nearly two decades has exited to establish an independent firm working with Indivisible Partners, a platform for independent advisor practices. The Baltimore-based team is establishing its own wealth management firm, Rosenwald Private Wealth.

Advisors should talk less, listen more. Here is a question to ask yourself before your next client meeting: At its end, will you have learned more about the client than they learned about you? Really getting to know clients by listening, as opposed to by displaying your expertise, is essential for success as an advisor, writes John Gatewood, the founder of the Gatewood Group. Here's the right sequence of events for client meetings: Establish a personal connection, make sure you understand their life story, and then provide your solutions, he writes.

Webull shares get slammed. Webull's stock took a beating last week, falling 19% the day after a congressional report criticized the company's ties to China. Last Friday, however, a Scotiabank analyst indicated the stock is a buy and said the company's remedies for addressing congressional concerns may not be that onerous. The stock has recovered some of its losses but is still down 18% in the past month.

data.title: AI Has Driven Bond Yields Higher, Says JPMorgan's Priya Misra — Sees Bonds As Hedge Against AI Trade
data.description:
Key points:
  • JPMorgan's Misra said AI-driven competition for capital and economic resilience helped push bond yields higher.
  • She viewed the market's pricing-in of three additional Fed rate hikes as overdone, while considering one or two reasonable.
  • Misra warned that sufficiently high real interest rates could cause something to break, pointing to leverage across financial markets.

Artificial intelligence (AI) investment has helped push bond yields higher, but JPMorgan Asset Management's Priya Misra sees high-quality fixed income as a potential hedge if momentum in the AI trade fades.

Speaking to Bloomberg Television on Friday, the Core Plus Bond ETF portfolio manager attributed the rise in rates partly to economic resilience and AI-driven competition for capital.

She noted that much of the increase in longer-term yields reflected higher real interest rates rather than inflation expectations. Misra also argued that much of the competition for capital and the higher cost of borrowing were already reflected in bond prices.

The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield stood at around 5.09% on Friday morning, down from approximately 5.24% at the end of the previous week, amid a rally in government bonds as AI-related stocks came under pressure.

Misra Says Markets Have Overpriced Fed Hikes

Misra viewed the bond market's pricing-in of additional Federal Reserve rate hikes as overdone, noting that markets were pricing in three hikes even as the Fed was discussing one or two more, which she considered reasonable.

On inflation, she attributed much of the pressure to supply shocks, citing the continuing effects of tariffs and oil prices. Misra also described AI as a structural demand shock, noting that AI demand was not particularly price-sensitive, while its supply-side effects would emerge later.

She also cautioned that sufficiently high real interest rates could cause something to break, pointing to leverage in the financial system and noting that not everyone had unrestricted access to capital.

Why Misra Still Sees Treasuries As A Safe Haven

Misra maintained that U.S. Treasuries remain a safe-haven asset, citing demand for German government bonds, known as bunds, during the recent sell-off in French government debt.

She cited government bond liquidity and governments' ability to raise taxes or reduce spending as factors supporting sovereign debt's safe-haven appeal.

Despite a difficult year for bonds, fixed income continued to attract inflows, which Misra partly attributed to the income cushion offered by elevated yields. She viewed high-quality fixed income yielding 6% to 7% as attractive and a potential hedge against weakness in the AI trade.

Treasury-Focused ETFs In Focus

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT), which tracks longer-dated U.S. government bonds, and the iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF (IEF), which provides exposure to intermediate-term Treasuries, were both trading marginally lower at the time of writing.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment toward both TLT and IEF remained in 'bullish' territory, accompanied by high message volume.

See Also: IMF Chief Says AI Is Strengthening Global Economy — But Warns Delayed Productivity Gains Could Trigger Shocks

data.title: Microsoft Stocks Slip Although $600 Target Meets an Unfinished AI Model
data.description:
Microsoft, the cloud and enterprise-software group , faces a clear test: turn stronger in-house AI into stronger business returns. The October 16 quote of $536.545 puts shares down approximately 0.54% against the $539.44 previous close listed by Stock Analysis, although the updated quote has no verified intraday timestamp. The Fly reported that StoneX analyst Yi Fu Lee raised his price target to $600 from $525 and maintained Buy. That is a bigger valuation call. Microsoft still needs to deliver the operating results behind it.

Microsoft disclosed on October 15 that MAI-Base-2 has completed pre-training, with 2.8 trillion total parameters and 80 billion active parameters. The company says it trained the model using 16,000 GB200 GPUs over 38 days. Those figures show the scale of the effort. They do not establish commercial availability, paying demand or lower costs for serving customers. Owning more of the model pipeline could give Microsoft greater control over its AI products and economics, but the financial payoff remains an execution question.

The valuation snapshot places shares 9.58% below the $593.39 GF Value estimate, suggesting a valuation cushion rather than a guaranteed return. StoneX's target increase is 14.3%; that measures the change in its target, not expected earnings growth. The next hurdle is concrete: deploy the technology into paid workloads and show what happens to revenue, margins and cash flow. Better model performance strengthens the technology case. Investors need evidence that it strengthens the business case, too.

data.title: CoreWeave leads AI-related stocks lower during Friday free fall
data.description:
CoreWeave led AI-related stocks into the red during a Friday free fall affecting much of the tech sector.

CoreWeave shares had declined nearly 12% by early afternoon trading. The AI data center company has plunged 34% over the past 10 days. The declines reflect a growing concern among investors that the AI infrastructure boom could become increasingly difficult to finance, particularly if inflation keeps interest rates elevated and customers struggle to generate sufficient returns on their investments.

Fellow neocloud, Nebius, shed 11%. Its share value has collapsed nearly 33% over the past 10 days. IREN declined 10%. It has collapsed 34% since October 6, following the same downward spiral as CoreWeave and Nebius over that time frame.

Hardware providers were also feeling the pain on Friday, as evidenced by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index sinking 2.8%. Micron fell 4%, AMD dropped 5%, and Intel declined 4.9%. Nvidia held on better, inching down 1%. Its share value has lost 10% since October 6.

Networking and optical shares were sinking as well. Lumentum declined 4%, Coherent dropped 6% and Celestica slid 3.5%.

While financing and fears of inadequate future revenue generation are prompting much of the sell-offs, the AI infrastructure buildout appears to remain unabated. Evidence for this appeared in TSMC's latest quarterly earnings report, which was released on Thursday.

Interestingly, analog and mixed-signal semiconductor stocks have remained more resilient. Texas Instruments inched up 0.4% on Friday. Analog Devices was relatively flat, and Onsemi was down 1%. Although these have all declined since October 6, the drops have not been as pronounced.

Software was not exempt from Friday's bleeding. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF had declined nearly 5% by afternoon trading.

A pullback in AI-related stocks has weighed on the broader market this week, with memory chip stocks among the hardest-hit segments as investors reassessed the sector's recent performance. SK Hynix fell 5.7% on Friday.

data.title: American Airlines Q3 preview: What guidance says about fuel-cost risks
data.description:
American Airlines heads into its October 22 earnings report with a key challenge: turning strong revenue growth into better profitability.

Wall Street expects a loss of $0.33 per share on revenue of $16.20B, while analysts have issued 18 downward EPS revisions and no upward revisions over the past three months.

The company’s third-quarter guidance highlights the pressure. American Airlines expects revenue to rise 16%–19% YoY, with available seat miles increasing 3%–5%.

However, it forecasts an adjusted loss of $0.70–$0.10 per share and a 2.5%–4.5% increase in non-fuel unit costs. Its fuel-price assumption was approximately $3.75 per gallon, based on the July 21 forward curve.

The full-year outlook also reflects the fuel burden. The company now expects adjusted EPS between a loss of $0.65 and a profit of $0.65 per share, citing higher fuel costs. Further increases in fuel prices could put additional pressure on earnings.

The second-quarter results showed why revenue growth has not translated into stronger profits. Revenue climbed 16.3% YoY to a record $16.74B, but operating expenses climbed 22.9% to $16.29B.

Fuel expense surged 83.3% to $4.88B, while operating income fell 60.7% to $446M. Adjusted EPS dropped to $0.15 from $0.95 a year earlier.

The company also recently warned that elevated jet fuel prices would push its third quarter results below the midpoint of guidance.

The airline is also trying to strengthen customer loyalty. Its new cash-and-miles booking option gives AAdvantage members more flexibility, while a planned Starlink rollout across its mainline fleet could improve the onboard experience from 2027.

Despite these initiatives, the company continues to face a profitability gap with larger rivals Delta Air Lines and United Airlines . Investors will be looking for signs that management can control costs and convert revenue growth into stronger earnings.

On the market side, the shares traded near $11.99 on Friday, down 21.17% year to date, while the S&P 500 (SP500) gained 13.13%.

Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating for the stock is 'Hold' at 3.21, with A+ grades for valuation and growth but a D+ grade for earnings revisions.

data.title: Angola's fuel subsidies spending projected to hit $4 billion in 2026, official says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Middle East war drives up Angola's spending on fuel subsidies
  • Oil prices expected to average around $90/bbl this year
  • Plans for external financing dependent on 2027 budget
  • Government actively opening up domestic bond market to foreign investors

By Rae Wee

Angola could spend up to 3.8 trillion kwanzas ($4.16 billion) on fuel subsidies this year, nearly double its initial projections of less than 2 trillion kwanzas, a senior finance official told Reuters on Friday.

The increase underscores the fiscal strain facing the oil-producing nation, as surging energy prices from the ongoing war in the Middle East drive up the cost of keeping domestic fuel prices low.

The mounting bill is adding pressure on the government to accelerate its gradual removal of subsidies, which began in 2023, but authorities are wary of moving too quickly for fear of economic and social fallout, Ottoniel dos Santos, Angola's secretary of state for finance and the treasury, told Reuters.

"We need to move not only with the subsidies removal, but also with the diversification of our economy," said dos Santos in an interview on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank ​in Bangkok.

"For now, it's been taken as it is - slowly," he added, referring to the scaling back of subsidies. "But if there is any window that could be used... and if we expect the impact on those who are more vulnerable are less than we forecast, then it will be easy to implement."

The country now expects oil prices to average around $90 per barrel by the end of the year, higher than the reference price of $61 it used in its 2026 budget.

Although the government has yet to submit its 2027 budget, due at the end of the month, dos Santos said its oil price assumption would not differ significantly from the International Monetary Fund's forecast of $71.50 a barrel.

The government expects crude production to come in at 1.045 million barrels per day in 2027, matching this year's output.

DIVERSIFYING FUNDING NEEDS

Angola's $4 billion Eurobond issuance and other liability operations have covered the "majority" of the country's funding needs this year, dos Santos said, with any plans for further bond issuances or external financing dependent on the 2027 budget.

"This is something that we will have to see what will be the needs for 2027 and identify if there is an opportunity or not for us to come back to the market," he told Reuters, adding that the country is actively opening up its domestic government bond market to foreign investors.

The government is welcoming "all investors, all the regions" to buy Angolan debt, and is stepping up efforts to educate investors on access to its capital market.

"Some investors think that the capital account is still closed, that it'll be difficult to get out when they get in, but actually it's not happening," said dos Santos.

"We want to go everywhere, we want them to come as well... we want people to know that Angola is opening the domestic market to get opportunities from other investors, from other countries."

($1 = 913.0000 kwanzas)

data.title: 453% return in 3 yrs: Multibagger stock declares bonus shares; do you own it? Check ratio, stock return and record date

data.title: Oberoi Realty Q2 results, dividend 2026: Check amount, record date, yield, history, stock returns
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- Real estate developer Oberoi Realty announced a reward for shareholders by declaring a second interim dividend of Rs.2 per share for FY27, alongside its financial results for the September quarter on Friday, October 16.

"This is to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on October 16, 2026, has declared the second interim dividend for FY27 at the rate of Rs.2 (Rupees Two only) per equity share, i.e., 20% of the face value of equity shares of Rs.10 each," the company said in its regulatory filing.

The company also fixed Friday, October 23, as the record date to determine shareholders' eligibility for the dividend payment. The dividend payment will commence on October 30, 2026, for eligible shareholders.

Investors looking to benefit from the payout must ensure they purchase the stock in time to be eligible for the dividend. Under India's T+1 settlement cycle, shares purchased on or after the record date will not qualify for the dividend.

In the past 12 months, Oberoi Realty has declared an equity dividend amounting to Rs.8 per share. At the current share price of Rs.1703, Oberoi Realty's dividend yield is 0.47%.

Oberoi Realty follows a quarterly dividend payout policy, distributing a portion of its profits to shareholders and offering them an opportunity to earn regular income alongside potential capital appreciation.

For the September quarter (Q2FY27), the company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs.761.65 crore, a marginal increase from Rs.760.26 crore in the year-ago period.

Total income fell 6% to Rs.1,736.37 crore during the second quarter of FY27 from Rs.1,844.84 crore in the corresponding period of the preceding fiscal, according to a regulatory filing.

The company's expenses declined to Rs.744.94 crore from Rs.863.35 crore, helping it register marginal profit growth during the July-September quarter of FY27.

During the first half of FY27, the company's net profit rose to Rs.1,305.16 crore from Rs.1,181.51 crore in the year-ago period. Total income increased to Rs.3,098.06 crore from Rs.2,918.82 crore.

Mumbai-based Oberoi Realty is one of India's leading real estate developers, primarily focusing on the development of luxury homes.

The company's shares have remained highly volatile in 2026, swinging between gains and losses amid weak broader market sentiment. The stock is up just 2% so far this year but has recovered 22% from its 52-week low.

After delivering positive returns for six consecutive years, the stock crashed 28% in 2025. From its record high of Rs.2,325, the stock has fallen 27% to Rs.1,703.

data.title: Why the Diesel Crisis Lifting Inflation Is Here to Stay — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Avi Salzman

The diesel shortage isn't going anywhere. Despite a frenzy of activity to boost supplies, some experts expect it to last into 2027, lifting global inflation for months.

"Diesel is gonna continue to be a huge problem for some time," said Dan Yergin, the Vice Chairman of S&P Global and a Pulitzer Prize-winning energy historian, in an interview on Friday. "Certainly for the next two months, you're not gonna see much impact because the system is disrupted. There will be marginal increases, but not on the scale that will alleviate what is a global problem."

The International Energy Agency predicted this week that supplies will be constrained "well into 2027." Even if refineries are able to pump out more fuel, countries will be in a rush to restore their depleted stockpiles, keeping prices elevated.

President Donald Trump is trying all sorts of methods to bring down the price of the fuel, which is particularly important for trucking and farming, and heating oil in the winter. Diesel prices have hit records around the world in the past few weeks, because of a shortage sparked by the wars in Russia and Iran, and exacerbated by a decline in diesel exports from China.

In the U.S., diesel cost an average of $6.33 a gallon at the pump on Friday, down only marginally from the record high of $6.53 it hit last month, according to AAA. Last year, a gallon cost $3.65.

The global diesel deficit in September was at 1 million barrels per day, according to JP Morgan, as the diesel trade fell to 6.1 million barrels from 7.1 million a year earlier.

Trump has turned to extraordinary measures, including making a deal with Russia and removing federal taxes on diesel used in trucking. But energy experts don't expect those efforts to result in much more diesel making it to buyers. Russia has officially imposed a diesel export ban, but has still been exporting about 140,000 barrels per day, down from over 700,000 in normal times.

Natasha Kaneva, the chief global commodities strategist at JP Morgan, thinks Trump's deal with Russia may simply formalize Russia's existing exports without adding supply. In fact, by her count the agreed-upon volumes that Russia can export are below what it's been sending out.

"Under the agreement, Russian diesel exports are set at 75,000 barrels per day in October and 125,000 in November," she writes.

A decision by European countries to tap into their strategic stockpiles could be more effective, as would any move by China to start exporting more, Kaneva notes.

"France announced the release of 10 million barrels from its strategic reserves, while Germany committed to an additional 15 million," Kaneva added. "Released over October and November, this combined volume would equate to 500,000 barrels per day and would cover roughly 50% of the current diesel deficit."

But whether those countries will quickly empty their reserves remains unknown. They have in the past been reluctant to do so, even after announcing decisions, Kaneva writes.

Diesel prices have broad impacts on the economy, because trucks and farm equipment run on diesel. When prices rise, the increases flow through to the price of food and other goods.

Middle Eastern countries have also been unable or unwilling to export diesel even as they've increased exports of crude from the Strait of Hormuz.

One problem is that Iranian attacks have hit their refineries. It also can be trickier to export fuel than crude, given that crude has more access to pipelines that bypass danger zones.

Yergin was in Saudi Arabia for a petroleum conference this week and said that state oil companies are having trouble exporting their fuel.

"The other major countries from the Gulf region were there, and people can't get product out," he said.

Until they can, the diesel premium could be here to stay.

Write to Avi Salzman at avi.salzman@barrons.com

data.title: CoreWeave Stock Tumbles Again -- Cantor Fitzgerald Sees a $176 Comeback
data.description:
The outlook for independent AI cloud providers is becoming a concern for investors, with Gartner projecting that 80% could lose their independence by 2030. Cantor Fitzgerald, however, sees improving economics at CoreWeave as a reason to remain bullish.

CoreWeave fell more than 7% in Friday morning trading, following a decline of over 15% on Wednesday. Rising borrowing costs have intensified market scrutiny of companies spending heavily to build AI computing capacity.

Cantor analyst Brett Knoblauch retained his Overweight rating and $176 price target. He estimates that almost all CoreWeave capacity scheduled to come online in 2027 has already been booked, while Nvidia has agreed to cover capacity that remains unsold.

The company's estimated revenue per megawatt has increased to about $20 million from $10 million to $11 million around its public listing. Knoblauch also estimates deal contribution margins have climbed to 25% to 30% from roughly 15%, shortening the time needed to recoup chip costs to 2 to 2.5 years from four years.

CoreWeave relies on asset-backed financing, with repayments supported by cash generated from its chips. Investors must weigh those improving returns against the borrowing needed to fund further expansion.

data.title: Trump says Zacharia should reconsider White House spokeswoman role
data.description:
By Trevor Hunnicutt and Jasper Ward

US President Donald Trump said on Friday he told new White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia she should reconsider her role after facing public scrutiny a week after taking the job.

"I told her: 'I think you're better off being happy, and I'm not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.' There's nothing easy about this stuff," Trump told reporters.

He added: "I said to her honestly, 'If I were you, I'd reconsider... think about it. But I would reconsider.'"

Fox News, citing a White House official, later reported that Zacharia was "transitioning" out of the role of press secretary.

Zacharia held her debut White House briefing on Tuesday.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Zacharia had said she received a call about the role of press secretary last Wednesday and got offered the job to succeed Karoline Leavitt last Friday.

Trump later announced her appointment. In his announcement, he described her an attorney.

Over the last week, the issue of whether Zacharia, a graduate of California's Pepperdine University law school, had actually passed the bar - making her an attorney - came under fire.

On Friday, during a Fox News interview on Thursday, Zacharia said she did not pass the bar.

Anthony Scaramucci served director of communications for 10 days during Trump's first administration.

data.title: Why CoreWeave is in the crosshairs of the AI scare
data.description:
Key points:
  • CoreWeave at fore of AI selloff, stocks and bonds plunge
  • Data center delays, revenue projections raise risks for neoclouds
  • Huge debt and losses mean CoreWeave is vulnerable

By Vidya Ranganathan and Aditya Soni

Loss-making and deeply indebted US cloud company CoreWeave became an easy target this week for investors concerned about an artificial intelligence bubble. Its selloff, though, has greater significance for markets than its size implies.

The slump in the shares and bonds of the $39 billion Nvidia-backed AI infrastructure company came after third-quarter reports from hyperscalers hinted at delays in data center projects and a slower pace of growth in capital expenditure.

Worried investors took aim at new-age AI-based cloud firms, or neoclouds, such as CoreWeave, conceivably the weakest links in the AI ecosystem because of how they borrow heavily to finance chips, land and energy for data centers which will yield income only in the future.

CoreWeave's shares dived more than 15% this week while yields on its 2030 bonds (21873SAB4=) jumped 500 basis points to near 16%.

CoreWeave chief Mike Intrator told employees in a memo, seen by Reuters, markets can sometimes "misunderstand and act irrationally" and it has a strong pipeline of demand. The company did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

Investors focused instead on its $50 billion debt and the perils of being trapped in the middle of a circular financing arrangement between chipmakers such as Nvidia and clients such as Meta Platforms and OpenAI.

"The problem with this stuff is that we're talking about huge interconnectedness, not just circular financing but the fact that these assets are all held in the same places, in the same portfolios, by the same types of investors," said James Athey, fixed-income portfolio manager at Marlborough.

"And leverage is always that thing which turns a storm into a teacup into something more nefarious," he said, referring broadly to the AI jitters.

Companies such as CoreWeave, Nebius , Applied Digital , Iren , Lambda Labs, Crusoe and TeraWulf are building energy-intensive data centers they can eventually rent out to firms developing and running AI models. That calls for massive upfront investment and very little income until the leases begin.

CoreWeave has never turned a profit, according to data compiled by LSEG.

CoreWeave's CEO also said in the memo that its deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations. The company had a $104.2 billion revenue backlog at the end of the second quarter, followed by more than $25 billion in new commitments early in the third quarter.

But the New Jersey-based company is burning cash faster than investors like. In 2025, CoreWeave reported annual revenue of $5.1 billion and a net loss of $1.2 billion.

While revenue is expected to double this year, capital expenditure is estimated to be up fourfold to between $35 billion and $39 billion, leading to even more cash burn this year. News that Intrator and entities linked to him have sold nearly $1 billion of stock since the company's IPO in March last year, mostly under prearranged trading plans as per regulatory filings, has not helped.

"Clearly they will need a capital injection or a bailout. They are burning capital, and capital is no longer free," said Alberto Gallo, founder of hedge fund Andromeda Capital.

"You want to buy debt in businesses that have visible cash flow, typically as a bond investor, not someone that is doing capex, in the hope that there will be more capex needed in the future," he said. The firm holds bets against CoreWeave bonds.

DOUBTS APLENTY

CoreWeave is at the top of the 100-odd neoclouds that research firm Gartner Inc says are "the most exposed to the imbalance between revenue and capital spending" and need to soon earn returns to sustain operations.

Gartner expects that by 2030, 80% of neocloud providers will cease independent operations.

"We are in a situation in which there are a lot of expectations on revenues and revenue growth, but this revenue growth is being fueled by the wrong type of capital, which is debt, not equity," said Tommaso Leodari, Dubai-based chief investment officer of hedge fund Index & Cie. The fund does not hold stakes in pure AI firms.

"In the specific case of CoreWeave, these guys are financing their entire business with debt. So if anything happens in the utilization of this particular asset or if there is a slowing down on the construction of these data centers, it will reflect in problems in repaying the debt."

A streak of warnings from AI hyperscalers such as Microsoft and Oracle Corp on delays in data center projects, power and component bottlenecks, a glut in high-end chips, alongside plans by giants such as Meta and Microsoft to launch their own chips to rival Nvidia's, have also stoked concerns about neoclouds.

The pace at which revenue is growing at AI giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic, while still fast, has also softened.

"Even at $10 billion revenue, CoreWeave is losing $2.5 billion, so there are no scale effects in the industry clear as yet," wrote Michael Frazis of Sydney-based Frazis Capital Partners.

CoreWeave has Nvidia's backing. The chip giant has agreed to buy unsold CoreWeave compute capacity through April 2032, guaranteeing it will have a buyer for capacity not sold to customers.

Ratings agencies have CoreWeave's debt marked as speculative grade, yet Sean Cray, vice president at Moody’s Ratings, pointed out the company does not speculatively purchase chips and has multiple avenues for financing.

Originally a bitcoin miner, CoreWeave has still been an easy mark for punters, and hedge funds have been buying its junk-rated bonds for the high yield. The cost of insuring its debt against default climbed to about 1,200 basis points this week, signalling severe distress.

"CoreWeave's credit selloff risks becoming a self-fulfilling prophecy," wrote Saurav Sen at research firm Gimme Credit. "The concern is less whether customers want the capacity than whether CoreWeave can afford to deliver it."

data.title: Air Canada, United to Add New U.S.-Canada Routes in Expanded Partnership
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Air Canada and United Airlines will add new routes between the U.S. and Canada as part of an expanded partnership between the two airlines.

The Canadian airline will serve flights between Toronto and Louisville, Montreal and Indianapolis, and Edmonton and Newark, as well expand capacity on its route between Edmonton and San Francisco. The new routes are set to launch next summer.

United Airlines will boost its service to Canada with routes from Denver to Ottawa and Quebec City and seasonal service between Newark and St. John's. United also plans to increase capacity on its Washington, D.C.-Quebec City and Denver-Winnipeg routes.

The two airlines also agreed to renew and expand their Transborder Joint Business Agreement, originally signed in 2022. The companies have submitted an application for approval by Transport Canada, the government agency responsible for transportation policies and programs.

"Our schedule has grown every year since our transborder agreement was signed in 2022, and the new routes and flights we're announcing today further underscore our commitment to investing in Canada and making travel between our two countries easier," said Patrick Quayle, United senior vice president of Global Network Planning and Alliances.

More than 4.3 million people have flown jointly on United and Air Canada since the agreement, Air Canada said.

data.title: Apple Stocks Rise Although Doubling Macs Adds 47% More Throughput in Muse Test
data.description:
Apple, the device and computing-platform company , faces a practical test for running AI locally: how much extra computing power justifies buying more hardware? Shares traded at $343.795, up approximately 0.53%, after the 9:30 a.m. ET market open on October 16. The question for professional buyers is straightforward. Does adding more Macs deliver enough extra performance to justify the bill?

According to Macworld's analysis, Apple's research measured Muse Spark Open at 24.99 tokens per second on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios, versus 36.73 on four. The benchmark used tensor parallelization, four-bit precision, 8,192 input tokens and 128 generated tokens. Double the computers delivered roughly 47% more throughput. That is a meaningful improvement, but buyers cannot assume performance rises in step with hardware spending.

Faster initial responses could strengthen the case, alongside privacy and the ability to handle demanding workloads locally. Still, one specialized benchmark does not establish a broad Mac sales opportunity. Valuation raises the bar: the $343.795 share price sits 19.1% above the $288.67 GF Value estimate, leaving less room for disappointing execution. Investors need evidence of professional customers buying these configurations repeatedly before treating local AI as a major new hardware growth engine.

data.title: Oil Futures Rise on Middle East, Russia-Ukraine Concerns — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid and Anthony Harrup

Oil prices turned higher Friday as Ukraine renewed attacks on Russian refineries, adding to concerns about persistent Middle East supply risks and uncertainty over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude for December delivery was up 3.2% at $109.28 a barrel, and December West Texas Intermediate gained 2.2% to $98.59 a barrel. Front-month WTI for November was up 2.8% at $100.71 a barrel, topping the $100 mark for the first time in a month.

"The main reason is that Ukraine has renewed its attacks on Russian oil refineries," said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital. "Despite the IEA and its member countries having already released approximately 300 million barrels from emergency oil reserves, with another 100 million barrels likely to be released, prices continue to rise."

The International Energy Agency said Thursday that its members agreed to accelerate the release of around 100 million barrels of previously pledged emergency oil stocks, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel to be released as soon as possible.

About 330 million barrels have already been released, and the agency said total releases would exceed the 400 million barrels initially agreed upon in March, with some members contributing additional volumes.

"We're still in a bull market," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of trading at BOK Financial. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz aren't reliable, expectations of Russian diesel coming onto the market aren't being met, and with Ukrainian attacks on refineries "those barrels are going to have trouble getting to the market," he said.

A third factor is that demand destruction "at least in the U.S. is not happening," he added.

Despite recovering Middle East oil flows, uncertainty surrounding the conflict continues to support crude prices, analysts at ING said. The bank said a sustained recovery in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz could gradually reduce the geopolitical risk premium, but a U.S.-Iran agreement would be needed to give markets greater confidence that higher flows could be maintained.

However, oil prices above $100 a barrel appear increasingly stretched relative to market fundamentals, according to Norbert Rucker, head of economics and next generation research at Julius Baer. Middle Eastern exports have largely recovered and global inventories remain comfortable, while geopolitical risk premiums and elevated freight costs could ease, he said.

"The relative calm in oil markets seems untenable, as the gradual recovery in Middle East oil flows has come under pressure of late from a resurgence of attacks on shipping," Barclays analyst Amarpreet Singh said in a note. "What looked like a tail risk scenario a few weeks ago--in which a diplomatic resolution takes us back to pre-war levels of Middle East supply and spare capacity--looks an even more remote possibility at this point," he added.

Shipping risks remain high after two cargo ships sank near the Strait of Hormuz following attacks, The Wall Street Journal reported. U.K. Maritime Trade Operations separately reported Wednesday that two container ships were struck by unidentified projectiles while transiting the waterway.

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com and Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Irish public sector trade unions suspend second day of strikes
data.description:
Irish public sector trade unions suspended a second day of widespread strikes planned for next week after they agreed on Friday to begin mediated discussions with the government this weekend on the terms for new pay talks.

Much of Ireland's public sector including teachers, health workers and civil servants on Wednesday staged the country's first major strike in almost two decades after failing for months to agree with ministers on the basis for negotiations on pay rises.

The two sides agreed on Friday to begin a process aimed at finding a basis for formal negotiations to commence.

"I believe that there is now a prospect of progress in the process that has been established. Obviously we will need to see the government's words backed up in practice," Kevin Callinan, chair of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions public services committee, told national broadcaster RTE.

data.title: BIRK Stock Downgraded By Williams Trading – Firm Believes ‘Lack Of Compelling New Product’ Is Affecting Demand
data.description:
Key points:
  • Williams Trading said sell-through rates are slowing in the Americas, while EMEA faces a disconnect between sell-in and sell-through, most evident at Zalando, according to Investing.com.
  • The firm said a “lack of compelling new product” is beginning to prompt wholesale partners in the Americas to pull back, according to The Fly.
  • Raymond James lowered its price target to $42 from $52 but maintained ‘Outperform’, citing DTC growth, EMEA performance, wholesale orders and product diversification.

Birkenstock (BIRK) shares were in focus on Friday after Williams Trading and Raymond James lowered their price targets on the stock.

According to The Fly, Williams Trading cut its price target to $27 from $39 and downgraded Birkenstock to ‘Sell’ from ‘Hold,’ saying the company’s fiscal 2028 targets will not be met. Raymond James lowered its target to $42 from $52 but maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating.

BIRK stock traded 4.3% lower at the time of writing.

Williams Trading Flags Promotional Activity, Wholesale Caution

According to The Fly, Williams Trading said Birkenstock’s fiscal 2028 targets will not be met. The firm noted that promotional activity is increasing, especially in Europe, and many of the company’s most loyal wholesale accounts in the Americas are adopting a more tempered approach to their 2027 plans.

Williams Trading also said a “lack of compelling new product” is beginning to cause wholesalers to step back in the Americas, The Fly reported.

Separately, according to a report published by Investing.com, Williams Trading said sell-through rates are decelerating in the Americas, although the market remains clean. In EMEA, the firm said there is a disconnect between sell-in and sell-through, most evident at Zalando.

Williams Trading noted it would not be surprised if Birkenstock tempers its fiscal 2028 targets when fourth-quarter earnings are announced later next month. Birkenstock’s fiscal 2028 outlook calls for revenue of €3.02 billion ($3.40 billion) to €3.183 billion ($3.58 billion) and a three-year constant-currency revenue CAGR of 13% to 15%, according to the report.

Raymond James Cites Growth And Product Diversification

Raymond James cited accelerating direct-to-consumer (DTC) growth, strong EMEA performance, healthy wholesale orders and product diversification as factors supporting Birkenstock’s fourth-quarter guidance and fiscal 2027 EPS of €2.53, according to The Fly.

The firm said the earnings per share (EPS) forecast represents 28% year-over-year growth and is above consensus. Store expansion, e-commerce improvements and lower tariffs were also cited as drivers of potential upside.

Retail View On BIRK

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment toward Birkenstock remained ‘Bearish’, while message volume was ‘Normal’ over the past 24 hours.

BIRK shares have dropped over 18% year-to-date.

(Exchange Rate: €1 = $1.13)

data.title: Clients Are Cheating on Their Financial Advisors. With AI. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kenneth Corbin

For all the talk about the potential for artificial intelligence to replace financial advisors, a new survey suggests an alternative scenario — that clients will use AI as a second opinion. Americans who use an advisor are far more likely to consult AI for financial advice than those who don't, according to the poll, fielded by Evergreen.ai, an AI-powered financial advice and planning app.

In a recent poll of nearly 2,000 Americans, Evergreen found that almost 64% of those who have a financial advisor said that they have asked AI about money issues. Among respondents who don't use a human advisor, that figure dropped to 38.5%.

Among all survey participants, 48.4% said that they have asked an AI chatbot about their finances in the past year. Of those who did, nearly 78% said they acted on the response they received.

"Americans are desperately seeking financial guidance," says Evergreen founder and CEO Bill Harris. "They are looking for answers wherever they can find them."

The survey showed that some respondents are using AI independently from their advisor. The participants with an advisor were far more likely to act on an AI-generated recommendation without researching it than those without an advisor. Evergreen concludes that "rather than replacing professional advice, AI appears to be layering on top of it, often without the same scrutiny."

That finding could be a product of so-called hybrid clients, those who work with an advisor who oversees a managed account while also maintaining a separate, self-directed account.

The survey also uncovered some familiar patterns, such as the lower confidence reported by respondents without an advisor compared with those who work with a financial professional.

Retirement uncertainty. Respondents indicated uncertainty around retirement planning and hesitancy to make major financial decisions. More than 42% of survey participants said that they had never bothered to estimate how much money they will need for retirement. Of those, nearly one-third said they expect to retire within 15 years.

Almost 90% of respondents said that they had put off at least one financial matter longer than they should have in the past year, with more than half saying they don't know where to start or that they have difficulty understanding their options.

"People are making decisions about taxes, retirement, and their financial futures without always having the answers they need," Harris says. "A human advisor remains invaluable, especially for complex decisions, and more people deserve access to clear information along the way."

data.title: Microsoft is the only hyperscaler not forecast to dip into negative FCF in the next year
data.description:
Microsoft stands alone among major hyperscalers as the only one not forecast to dip into negative free cash flow territory over the next twelve months, according to BofA Global Research Equity and Quant Strategy.

Amazon , Alphabet , , Oracle , and Meta are all expected to fall into negative free cash flow by 2027, with BofA Global Research projecting these hyperscalers' next-twelve-month free cash flow estimates will drop below negative $25,000 between 2026 and 2028.

The outlook isn't entirely bleak for the sector, according to BofA Global Research, which expects hyperscalers' free cash flow to shift from negative to positive by the second half of 2027 as AI-related revenue growth accelerates and AI capital expenditures decelerate.

However, the research firm warns of significant risk: AI capex has surprised to the upside by a much wider margin than revenue—50% versus 20% this year—meaning 2027 expectations imply a marked shift in trend.

BofA Global Research's estimated compute demand through 2030 implies approximately $10T of spend, roughly $2T above current forecasts.

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq set for steep weekly losses as AI jitters rattle investors
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes down: Dow 0.03%, S&P 0.56%, Nasdaq 1.3%
  • Chips, neocloud companies slide as debt concerns linger
  • Gains in banks limit Dow's fall, set for weekly gains

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Purvi Agarwal

The benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end the week in the red, with technology stocks coming under more pressure on Friday over cracks in the AI trade and adding to losses.

The S&P 500 information technology index fell 1.5% and was the biggest drag. Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slid 10.3% on lingering debt concerns. The data centre operator's bonds sold off sharply this week, pushing yields to above 15%.

Semiconductors bore the brunt of the selloff, with the broader chips index dropping 1.8% — set for its steepest eight-session percentage decline since the "Liberation Day" selloff in April 2025.

Most megacap stocks tumbled and brought the Nasdaq close to a one-month low. Meta slipped 2.3% and Microsoft lost 1.8%.

AI stocks have cratered this week over concerns that data centre operators might not turn profitable in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise. Worries over rising competition from China also dented sentiment.

"When investors start worrying that AI names are overvalued, they gravitate toward lower-multiple stocks with stable cash flows," said Dennis Dick, founder and market structure analyst at Triple D Trading.

Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors are weighing a lower valuation for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

At 12:19 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 14.74 points, or 0.03%, to 52,162.95, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 43.53 points, or 0.56%, to 7,700.38 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 348.31 points, or 1.30%, to 26,364.72.

Most other S&P 500 sectors rose. The energy index was the biggest percentage gainer, up 1.5%, while the financials index rose 1%.

Gains in Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase lifted the Dow to its highest level in over a month. The index is set for a weekly advance, with investors rushing to defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples.

"What we're seeing now is money rotating out of a very crowded AI trade and into value names," Dick added.

The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since early June, faced with an AI-led rout, mixed bank earnings and inflation data. The Nasdaq eyed its sharpest weekly fall since June 22.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week have confirmed that price pressures are extending beyond energy products.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh also said a spending surge was boosting inflation, but added that the US economy remained resilient and benefited from the AI-driven investment boom.

Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays now expects 25 basis point hikes each in December and January.

Meanwhile, Tesla failed to hold on to gains from before the bell — as much as 3% — after unveiling a redesigned Roadster, powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX.

Netflix appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.6%.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.94-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and no new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 46 new highs and 200 new lows.

data.title: Micron Stocks Fall 3.5% Although Bullish Memory Commentary Meets a Cash Test
data.description:
Micron Technology, the memory and storage-chip producer , faces tougher questions about the durability of its memory boom, with shares at $898.77, down 3.5%, around 10:34 a.m. ET on October 16. According to Benzinga, Bernstein analyst Mark Newman sees value in memory stocks after their retreat, even as price increases lose momentum. Slower increases do not mean prices are falling. They do put more pressure on earnings growth to justify the investment story.

Micron's September 30 earnings release reported quarterly revenue of $54.229 billion and adjusted free cash flow of $33.199 billion. That is roughly 61.2 cents of adjusted free cash flow for every revenue dollar. Management's next-quarter sales forecast stands at $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion. The midpoint implies another 13.4% sequential increase. Cash gives Micron room to expand. Earning attractive returns on that expansion is the next test.

The valuation snapshot shows shares trading 14.63% above GF Value of $784.03, suggesting the pullback has not erased the premium to that estimate. Investors still need to weigh that premium against future growth. The Stock Analysis overview provides additional financial context, but the operating numbers deserve the closest watch: revenue, margins and capital spending. Strong cash generation can fund more production. Sustained demand and disciplined spending will determine whether that production creates lasting shareholder value.
